Garbage game. No one to play with online at lower difficulties so you'll have to play solo. You can try playing on a higher difficulty but the way the gameplay loop is set up you have to first play the levels through on normal difficulty to unlock power up cards you can equip so that you are strong enough for the later levels. The hilarious part of that is there really isn't any reason to replay levels other than to get more in game currency. This means the game is designed to make you want to replay levels not because they're fun but because it's the only way to level up. And the card system adds rng but it isnt fun. Why would i replay a level just to get absolutely clapped by a card draw of an ogre and armored monsters and also the ridden are on fire. 

Speaking of the ridden, they are not fun to kill. Standard ridden will swarm you but the game does such a poor job of telling you that you're being attacked from beind that you won't even notice until there's like 3 or 5 chompin yr bits. And the special ridden are so poorly designed. In a game where every level is go from point a to point b why is every ridden designed against that. For example, the tallboy and smasher both have their weakspots behind them. when you have one walking down the hall at you there is no outplay other than empty your mags into it and hope theres more ammo for the next one that will likely spawn withing seconds. Add the big dumb ones that explode into bile when they die, cutting off any forward progress, and it just feels like a punishment dealing with the special ridden rather than a fun game. Add a couple random cards in there so that they're weak spots are armored and it's nearly unplayable with random people online who will most likely stumble onto every pack of crows and alarm doors they can find.

the levels themselves are so repetetive. Idk why they set the game up this way. Each act is split into like 6-8 levels and each acct level starts in the same place and if it's not the same exact place it's something similar. it's 2022. Technology is so advanced rn. Turtle rock could have done whatever they wanted to do with these levels. in L4D2 you play a mission in new orleans, another in a carnival that ends in a rock concert, another mission in a spooky swampy bayou, and another in an airport which each level having a memorable and challenging final act with big set pieces and different challenges. In this game you get 25 variations of fort hope and the surrounding area, hallways, and then an extended "destroy nests to move on" segment. Even world war z has more memorable and unique levels.

I really wanted to give this game a chance even after all my friends dropped it due to the various launch problems it had. I got through most of the game until the final act where there is a boss fight that is dependet on shooting weakspots (surprise surprise). This one also has a timer. the game glitched halfway through the battle and stopped showing the locations of all the weak spots. i scurried around trying to find the last one but couldn't so the boss escaped. i could replay the entire boring level for 35 mintues or i can just uninstall and move on with my life and do anything else with my time. 

To be fair, l4d2 isn't fun to play solo but at least it's fun to play with friends and has active players online. Can't quite say the same for this. Definitely buy this if it's on such a steep sale that turtle rock sends you a check for downloading the game

This review is just a disorganized mess of my thoughts on the game. 
They fixed the card system and it's a lot of fun now. Ridden animations still suck compared to L4D, and the blood splatter on bullet hits is reeeeaally aggressive and makes it hard to see sometimes, but overall the game feels like a worthy successor now. Teamwork is rewarded. You can share ammo and money (if you want to) and the ping system makes communication a LOT easier. The AI is also helpful when playing solo or only with one or two friends. They will drop ammo for you when you run low and ping enemies. They cannot set off traps, car alarms, scare birds, or damage you. 
You can only unlock skins and cards by playing the game. No store buy options. You don't see much of that in AAA (AA?) titles these days. I admire that. Makes the mild grind feel worthwhile. I really like the gunplay. I have a shotgun deck setup with a lot of cards that increase movement speed, stamina, and prevent ADS, so it makes the game feel like Doom. Pretty sweet.
The levels are pretty well-detailed and the story is whatever, like every zombie game except TLOU. But this game is about the gameplay and screaming at your friends when they trigger a hoard. 
 Good ol' fun. 8/10. 100 hours in and I'm still unlocking new skins and cards. Play with your friends.
